cell phone.name: Cell Phone
cell phone.tip: Back up and factory-reset it, take out the SIM and memory card, then hand it to a certified take-back point.

laptop.name: Laptop
laptop.tip: Wipe your data securely and log out of all accounts. Reusable laptops are often better donated first.

tablet.name: Tablet
tablet.tip: Sign out of your accounts and factory-reset. A swollen battery means it must go to a hazardous-waste drop-off.

desktop computer.name: Desktop Computer
desktop computer.tip: Wipe or remove the hard drive first. RAM, drives and power supplies can often be reused before recycling.

monitor.name: Monitor
monitor.tip: Never smash or open the screen. Older CRT and LCD monitors need certified handlers.

tv.name: Television
tv.tip: Don't put it out with regular trash. Many retailers take old TVs back when you buy a new one.

keyboard.name: Keyboard
keyboard.tip: Unplug it and remove batteries if wireless. The plastics and metals are recoverable.

mouse.name: Computer Mouse
mouse.tip: Take out the batteries and recycle them separately. Bundle small peripherals for one drop-off.

printer.name: Printer
printer.tip: Remove ink or toner cartridges first. Many brands run free cartridge return programs.

charger.name: Charger / Adapter
charger.tip: Bundle cables and adapters together. The copper inside is highly recoverable.

battery.name: Battery
battery.tip: Tape the terminals, keep it dry and never put it in a household bin. Damaged batteries are a fire risk.

power bank.name: Power Bank
power bank.tip: Swollen or damaged? Keep it away from heat and take it to a hazardous-waste drop-off.

earphone.name: Earphones / Headphones
earphone.tip: Wireless earbuds contain tiny batteries, so they belong at an e-waste point, not in the bin.

speaker.name: Speaker
speaker.tip: Remove any batteries. The magnets and copper coils are valuable to recyclers.

camera.name: Camera
camera.tip: Take out the battery and memory card. Working cameras are great for donation or resale.

smartwatch.name: Smartwatch
smartwatch.tip: Unpair and factory-reset it. The sealed battery means it needs a proper e-waste drop-off.

remote control.name: Remote Control
remote control.tip: Remove the batteries and recycle them separately from the remote.

router.name: Router / Modem
router.tip: Factory-reset it first. Many internet providers will take old routers back for free.

hard drive.name: Hard Drive
hard drive.tip: Wipe it or use certified data destruction. Deleting files alone is not enough.

game controller.name: Game Controller
game controller.tip: Remove the battery pack if you can. Working controllers are easy to donate.

microwave.name: Microwave Oven
microwave.tip: Capacitors hold a charge even when unplugged, so don't open it. Ask your bulky-waste service for pickup.

refrigerator.name: Refrigerator
refrigerator.tip: A licensed handler must recover the refrigerant. Don't dismantle it. Many retailers haul the old unit away on delivery.

washing machine.name: Washing Machine
washing machine.tip: It's mostly steel, so scrap collectors and retailer take-back schemes will usually collect it.

electric fan.name: Electric Fan
electric fan.tip: Small appliances go to an e-waste point, not the bin. The motor's copper is recoverable.

hair dryer.name: Hair Dryer
hair dryer.tip: Take it to an e-waste collection point. The heating coil and motor contain reusable metals.
